beats.subline: Tuesday, November 17, 2026 close — a broad, tech-led selloff over new AI-chip export curbs, though Nvidia's earnings beat sparked an after-hours bounce.
beats.body: Nvidia posted record $115.8 billion in fiscal third-quarter revenue, up 103% year-over-year, and guided to roughly $130 billion next quarter in its first report since Jensen Huang's resignation; shares rose about 4.5% after hours. Salesforce sank 9.5% on fears AI will displace its software, and Anthropic's IPO — expected to price above its $70-$78 range Wednesday evening — added to AI-sector jitters.

beats.headline: Trump heads to Shenzhen for first-ever Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral after Manila stop
beats.body: President Trump met Philippine President Marcos and other ASEAN and Quad leaders in Manila this week before traveling on to Shenzhen for the APEC summit; the White House says Thursday's unprecedented three-way meeting with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin will focus on nuclear arms reduction, with the Iran war and US-China trade tensions also expected to come up.

beats.headline: China presses ahead with new South China Sea runway capable of hosting bombers
beats.body: Satellite imagery reviewed by analysts shows China building a nearly 3-kilometer runway on Antelope Reef in the Paracel Islands — a second strip there, expected to be operational by mid-2027 — that researchers say could host bombers and tankers and help Beijing restrict US and allied naval access in a crisis; Vietnam has called the construction illegal, and Australia's defense minister says the buildup is creating a 'condition of pressure' across Southeast Asia.

beats.headline: US warplanes strike Iranian missile site on Qeshm Island after drone attacks on Gulf bases
beats.body: US aircraft struck an Iranian missile-launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, which an official called self-defense after Iranian drones targeted American and Kuwaiti bases in Bahrain and Kuwait; Vice President Vance said Trump won't let the standoff become a 'forever war,' even as Trump separately warned Iran would 'pay a price' over a reported plot to smuggle a 'dirty bomb' into Washington.

beats.headline: Anthropic set to price its IPO above range Wednesday, valuing Claude's maker near $1.4 trillion
beats.body: Anthropic plans to price 825 million shares above its $70-$78 range after Wednesday's close, with 'ANT' shares opening on Nasdaq Thursday in the first US listing by a major AI lab; bankers say orders have run roughly seven times the shares on offer. The listing lands the same day Nvidia reported record $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue and guided to 75% revenue growth this fiscal year, underscoring continued AI infrastructure demand.
